solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No place for students with closed minds?

definitions.text: No place for students with closed minds?

parts.words: No place for students with closed minds?
parts.note: a British distance-learning institution is a college that is notionally unlocked to all, so it is no home for the narrow-minded

explanation.surface: A jibe that some college is unsuitable for blinkered undergraduates.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university with no entry requirements; the clue plays on 'open' as the opposite of 'closed minds'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes, cryptically, a university whose name declares it is never shut to anyone.

clue.text: Giving as one's view how longing follows love

indicators.note: follows places the longing word after the love letter in the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
longing means pining

explanation.surface: Someone describes how yearning comes after falling in love.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, so this verb form means expressing one's view.

clue.text: It uses current provision for comfortable retirement

definitions.text: It uses current provision for comfortable retirement

parts.words: It uses current provision for comfortable retirement
parts.note: current is electric current and retirement is going to bed, not a pension plan

explanation.surface: Sounds like a financial product that funds a pleasant old age from present income.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed-warming device runs on electricity and makes going to bed cosy.

clue.text: Part of Connecticut ahead, or another state

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Moving on from Connecticut to name a different American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'or another state' as the definition; 'or' is only a link, since 'another state' alone stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the United States, a different one from Connecticut.

clue.text: Container for black stuff changed to pink

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something holding a black substance has been turned pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' shuffles TO PINK.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pot of writing fluid, which is typically black, is exactly this container.

clue.text: Go up, perhaps, as special case, not before time

indicators.note: special, read as unusual or out of the ordinary, signals that the next word is rearranged

parts.note: something not before time is late

explanation.surface: A request treated as an exception, arriving after its deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' shuffles CASE into ESCA; 'as' is a link. 'perhaps' marks going up as one sense of the answer, which also means intensify.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to rise or increase, so going up is an example of it.

clue.text: Sound upset, but regrouping — that's very impressive

indicators.note: regrouping says the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sounds annoyed but is reorganising, and calls that remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal for 'Sound', but it is fodder too; 'regrouping' shuffles all ten letters of SOUND UPSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous is a synonym for astounding or extremely impressive.

clue.text: Contact info for person, booked earlier, now put in cell?

definitions.text: Contact info for person, booked earlier, now put in cell?

parts.words: Contact info for person, booked earlier, now put in cell?
parts.note: the surface suggests a criminal booked and jailed, but cell is a mobile phone storing contact details

explanation.surface: Details on a suspect who was booked and is now locked in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits you dial to reach someone, once noted in an address book and now stored in a mobile.

clue.text: Isis or, possibly, another Egyptian deity

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Naming a goddess, or maybe a different god of ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles ISIS OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and husband of Isis.

clue.text: Treatment for bruises, being in charge of English forwards

parts.note: in rugby the forwards are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: A rugby captain overseeing England's front row tends their knocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link. In rugby union the forwards are called the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of frozen material is applied to a bruise to reduce swelling.

clue.text: Pairs romantically entangled in close-up

indicators.note: entangled says the letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Lovers caught entwined in a close-up camera shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romantically entangled' shuffles CLOSE-UP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples are twos, especially romantic partners.

clue.text: Fascinated by aspects of Macintosh

indicators.note: aspects of says the answer is just part of the following word

explanation.surface: A fan enthralled by the features of an Apple computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspects of' picks a run of letters from inside MACINTOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is informal for being keen on or engrossed in it.

clue.text: After gaol has change of heart, guard becomes number one

indicators.note: the heart of the word gaol is its middle pair, and changing it swaps those two letters

parts.note: a guard is a keeper

explanation.surface: Leaving prison a reformed character, the warder rises to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' swaps the two middle letters of the British spelling of jail. 'After' and 'becomes' are links; a football goalkeeper wears shirt number one.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the goalkeeper traditionally wears the number 1 shirt.

clue.text: With careful consideration, put back into prison?

definitions.meaning: ... describes something done with thought and intent
playfully read as ..., undoing a liberation

explanation.surface: Thoughtfully returning someone to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate means considered and intentional; split as de-liberate it jokingly means reverse a release.

clue.text: Country valued more highly than sovereign once

definitions.text: valued more highly than sovereign once
definitions.meaning: an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, one more than the 20-shilling sovereign

explanation.surface: A nation that historically outranked its monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold coin worth one pound (20 shillings); the guinea was worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea is a West African republic and also an old coin worth a little more than a sovereign.

clue.text: Working hard as learner boss promises to pay

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A trainee works hard while the manager hands out IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not a manager but a raised ornamental stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious means devoted to study, which is what a diligent learner is.

clue.text: Child confused about period relating to display of arms

indicators.note: about means the muddled letters go around the period word
confused says the letters of the word child are muddled

parts.note: a period of history is an era

explanation.surface: A muddled youngster around a particular time, linked to a show of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' shuffles the child word and 'about' wraps it round the period. Arms here are coats of arms, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic means concerning heraldry, the design and display of coats of arms.

clue.text: Religious leader and Edward talked

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A rabbi and a man named Edward had a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbited is British slang for chattered or talked on and on.

clue.text: Provoke disgust about act, initially — thus annul it

indicators.note: about means the repel word goes around the extra letter

parts.note: to repel is to provoke disgust

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of act

explanation.surface: An offensive law should be struck down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A from 'act', which 'about' puts inside REPEL; 'thus' and 'it' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or cancel it.

clue.text: One and a third months in Northern state capital

parts.note: one of the months, here June

indicators.note: a third keeps two of the six letters, losing the rest

parts.note: another month, August

explanation.surface: Spending sixteen weeks or so in the capital of a far northern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' month is JUNE and 'a third' of a month is AU, the first third of AUGUST. Juneau is the capital of Alaska; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Juneau is the capital city of Alaska, the most northerly US state.

clue.text: Say line at end of play? Absolutely!

parts.note: to say is to utter

indicators.note: at end of takes the last letter of play

explanation.surface: An actor delivers the closing line of a play and is wholeheartedly agreed with.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly is an intensifier meaning completely or totally.

clue.text: Cleric converted group of friends

indicators.note: converted tells us the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A churchman changed faith and joined a social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks religious beside 'Cleric' but it shuffles that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a set of people with shared interests or friendship.

clue.text: Design part of opera around movie in which all the stars can be seen

definitions.text: in which all the stars can be seen

indicators.note: around means the design and opera words close round the movie

parts.note: a design is a plan
an aria is a solo song in an opera
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A stage set built round a film featuring every celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Plural 'planetaria' are domed theatres where the night sky is projected; 'stars' suggests film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetariums project the whole night sky, showing every star; the definition stands for places of that kind.

clue.text: Hardly fair

explanation.definitionFit: The word means barely (as in only just) and also equitable or right.

clue.text: Bear up, band

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: Endure and hold up a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear up' looks like a phrase meaning endure; it is POOH (Winnie-the-Pooh) going 'up' the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, such as a metal ring round a barrel.

clue.text: Embarrassing amount of power carried by prize

indicators.note: carried by means the power unit sits inside the prize word

parts.note: a prize is an award
kW, kilowatt, is a measure of power

explanation.surface: A large electricity bill delivered with a trophy causes blushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward can describe a situation causing embarrassment or unease.

clue.text: Belt is what one wears

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes or gear

explanation.surface: A waistband counts as an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British informal: clobber as verb is to hit, as noun one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber means to thump someone and is also slang for clothing and kit.

clue.text: Group helping patients with uplifting and moving performance

definitions.text: Group helping patients with uplifting and moving performance

parts.words: Group helping patients with uplifting and moving performance
parts.note: the uplifting and moving is literal: a team lifts the injured on a litter and carries them away

explanation.surface: A troupe cheers up hospital patients with an inspiring, emotional show.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of bearers who lift casualties on a litter and carry them to care.
